facts.text: The white-browed scrubwren is a small brown bird, 11–14 cm long, with prominent white brows and pale eyes.
facts.quote: It is 11–14 cm (4.3–5.5 in) long and predominantly brown in colour with prominent white brows and pale eyes

facts.text: Males have blackish lores while females have pale grey ones, so most birds can be reliably sexed in the field.
facts.quote: The females are duller overall and generally have pale gray lores, whereas males have blackish lores. This allows most individuals to be reliably sexed in the field.

facts.text: It has a loud, high-pitched call that sounds like ts-cheer or ch-weip, ch-weip, ch-weip.
facts.quote: The call is a loud high-pitched ts-cheer or ch-weip, ch-weip, ch-weip.

facts.text: Scrubwrens are hard to spot but very vocal, so you can easily localise them by ear.
facts.quote: They can be hard to spot but are very vocal and easy to localise.

facts.text: It lives in small groups of up to six birds, and all group members help feed and rear the young.
facts.quote: They occur in small groups of up to six birds and engage in cooperative breeding; namely that group members all help to feed and rear the young.

facts.text: It eats insects and stays hidden in undergrowth, though it can be found close to urban areas.
facts.quote: It is insectivorous and inhabits undergrowth, from which it rarely ventures, though can be found close to urban areas.

facts.text: The domelike nest, built near or on the ground in dense cover, is made of grasses, leaves, sticks, bark, ferns and feather lining.
facts.quote: the nest a domelike structure of dried grasses and leaves, sticks, bark and ferns and feathers for lining. It is placed near or on the ground in dense cover.

facts.text: It is a sedentary bird favouring forested or scrubby areas with plentiful undergrowth.
facts.quote: The species favours forested or scrubby areas with plentiful undergrowth, from which it rarely ventures. It is a common bird in bushland areas around Sydney, and the New England Tablelands. It is sedentary.
